mainTopic: The end of פרק במה מדליקין, and the opening of פרק כירה: when may a pot sit on a stove (כירה) on שבת, and what does the משנה's 'לא יתן' mean?
overview: This amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: knowing the correct name of בבל matters for writing a valid גט. Then the הדרן closes פרק במה מדליקין, and a new chapter begins with a משנה about a כירה (stove) on שבת. If the stove was heated with straw or stubble, a pot may be put on it. If it was heated with גפת or wood, the coals must first be swept out (גרוף) or covered with ashes (קטום). The משנה adds two מחלוקות between בית שמאי and בית הלל: hot water versus a cooked dish, and whether a pot that was taken off may be put back. The גמרא asks whether 'לא יתן' limits only putting a pot back on שבת (חזרה), as חנניה would hold, or also leaving it on from before שבת (שהייה). It tries to prove the answer from the fact that the משנה has two separate disputes. If the משנה were about returning, the second dispute would be a needless repeat, so the proof leans toward the שהייה reading. The גמרא examines this proof further on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the name of Babylon matters: for divorce documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier discussion about the changing names of בבל. It says the practical difference is for writing גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make? It matters for women's bills of divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a discussion from the previous page about places whose names changed. The גמרא asks why it matters and answers: for writing a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must name the place where it was written correctly. If a city's name changed, the scribe must know the right name to use. So a fact about geography turns out to matter for הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
For women's bills of divorce.
phrases.notes: A גט must record the place where it was written with its correct name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier sugya about the name changes of בבל (from the previous page).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Knowing a place's correct name matters for writing a valid גט.

steps.title: הדרן: closing the chapter במה מדליקין
steps.stepSummary: The traditional formula that marks the end of פרק במה מדליקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'With What May One Light'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the formula said when finishing a chapter, marking that פרק במה מדליקין is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן expresses a hope to come back and learn the chapter again. Everything after this belongs to a new chapter with a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
'With what may one light', the name of the second chapter of שבת

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'With What May One Light'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter in which step 1 appeared.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק במה מדליקין is finished; a new chapter begins.

steps.title: משנה: placing a pot on a stove depends on the fuel
steps.stepSummary: If a כירה was heated with straw or stubble, a pot may be put on it. If it was heated with גפת or wood, a pot may not be put on it until the coals are swept out or covered with ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A stove that was heated with straw or stubble: we may place a cooked dish on it. If it was heated with olive waste or wood: one may not place a dish on it until he sweeps out the coals, or until he puts ashes over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The new chapter opens with a משנה about putting food on a stove for שבת. The rule depends on what fuel heated the stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straw and stubble burn out fast and leave few live coals, so there is little worry. גפת and wood leave hot coals. Someone might stir them to cook the food more, which would be a מלאכה on שבת. Sweeping out the coals (גרוף) or covering them with ashes (קטום) removes that worry.

keyTerms.meaning: A stove that holds two pots
Stubble or scraps gathered from the field
Waste pulp left after pressing olives or sesame; burns very hot
That he sweeps out the coals

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the משנה only says 'לא יתן' (may not place). It does not say whether this means putting the pot back on during שבת, or leaving it on from before שבת. That exact question is what the גמרא asks below.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the root source for the laws of שהייה and חזרה, which govern keeping food warm on a stove on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A stove that they heated
with straw or with stubble,
we may place a cooked dish on it.
With olive waste or with wood,
one may not place it until he sweeps out the coals,
or until he puts ashes over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter (פרק כירה) with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straw or stubble: allowed. גפת or wood: only after גרוף or קטום.

steps.title: משנה: hot water versus cooked food
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow only hot water on such a stove, not a cooked dish. בית הלל allow both.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: hot water, but not a cooked dish. בית הלל say: both hot water and a cooked dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about what kinds of food may be put on the stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot water needs no more cooking, so no one will be tempted to stir the coals for it. A cooked dish often gets better with more cooking, so בית שמאי worry a person may stir the coals. בית הלל do not worry about this.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: hot water,
but not a cooked dish.
And Beit Hillel say: hot water and a cooked dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: חַמִּין, אֲבָל לֹא תַּבְשִׁיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a מחלוקת about which foods are allowed on the swept or covered stove.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: hot water only. בית הלל: hot water and a cooked dish.

steps.title: משנה: removing a pot and returning it
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow taking a pot off the stove on שבת but not putting it back. בית הלל allow putting it back too.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: we may remove it, but we may not return it. בית הלל say: we may even return it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second מחלוקת in the משנה, about taking a pot off the stove on שבת and putting it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a pot back on the fire during שבת (חזרה) looks more like a new act of cooking than leaving it there. בית שמאי forbid it. בית הלל permit it. The גמרא will later use the fact that the משנה has two separate מחלוקות to work out what 'לא יתן' means.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: we may remove it,
but we may not return it.
And Beit Hillel say: we may even return it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹטְלִין, אֲבָל לֹא מַחֲזִירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second מחלוקת, this time about putting a pot back on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: remove but do not return. בית הלל: one may even return.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: (1) the fuel rule with גרוף or קטום, (2) hot water versus a cooked dish, (3) removing versus returning.

steps.title: The question, first side: does 'may not place' mean only 'may not return'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'לא יתן' forbids only putting a pot back on שבת, while leaving it on from before שבת is allowed even on a stove that is not swept or covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: this 'one may not place', is it 'one may not return'? But to leave it on, we may leave it, even though the stove is not swept and not covered with ashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks an איבעיא about what the unclear words 'לא יתן' mean. This step gives the first possible reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the משנה's limit applies only to חזרה, putting a pot back during שבת. Leaving a pot on from before שבת (שהייה) would be allowed even on a hot stove that was not swept or covered. That is a lenient reading, so the גמרא will next look for which תנא could hold it.

keyTerms.meaning: To leave a pot on the fire from before שבת
He may not put it back

steps.confusionAlert: Keep two cases apart. שהייה means leaving a pot on the stove from before שבת. חזרה means putting a pot back on the stove during שבת. The whole question is which of these the משנה's 'לא יתן' refers to.

phrases.english: GEMARA: They raised a dilemma:
This 'one may not place': is it 'one may not return'?
But to leave it on, we may leave it,
even though the stove is not swept
and not covered with ashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הַאי לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא יַחֲזִיר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unclear wording 'לא יתן' in the משנה's first rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'לא יתן' refer only to חזרה (returning), or also to שהייה (leaving the pot on)?

steps.title: The first side matches the view of חנניה
steps.stepSummary: If the first reading is right, the משנה follows חנניה. He allows leaving food that is already cooked like the food of בן דרוסאי on a stove that is not swept or covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose view is this? It is חנניה's. As it was taught in a ברייתא, חנניה says: any food that is cooked like the food of בן דרוסאי may be left on a stove, even though the stove is not swept and not covered with ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside its question, the גמרא notes which תנא the first reading would follow: חנניה, quoted from a ברייתא. This shows the first side is a real option, but nothing is decided yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן דרוסאי was a robber who ate his food only partly cooked, about one third of the way. Once food reaches that level, חנניה is not worried that someone will stir the coals, so שהייה is allowed even on a hot stove. This shows the first reading fits a known opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Food cooked to the level בן דרוסאי ate it (partly cooked)

phrases.english: And whose view is it? It is Chananya's.
As it was taught: Chananya says:
Anything that is like the food of ben Drosai
may be left on top of a stove,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ גָּרוּף וְאֵינוֹ קָטוּם.
phrases.english: even though it is not swept and not covered with ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the תנא who would hold the first reading.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the משנה allows שהייה without גרוף or קטום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of חנניה about food cooked like the food of בן דרוסאי.

steps.title: The question, second side: 'may not place' means 'may not leave'
steps.stepSummary: Or perhaps the משנה is about שהייה. Leaving a pot on is allowed only on a swept or covered stove, and returning it is certainly forbidden otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps we learned the משנה about leaving the pot on. If the stove is swept or covered, yes. If not, no. And all the more so, one may not return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of its question. This reading is stricter, and the question stays open here, setting up the attempt to answer it that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, even שהייה needs a גרוף or קטום stove. Putting a pot back during שבת is a bigger step, so by a קל וחומר it is certainly forbidden on a stove that is not swept or covered.

phrases.english: Or perhaps we learned it about leaving the pot on,
and if it is swept or covered, yes,
if not, no,
and all the more so, not to return it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other possible reading of 'לא יתן', stricter than the first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'לא יתן' refers to שהייה, so that even leaving a pot on requires גרוף or קטום.
steps.whatToRemember: Two possible readings of 'לא יתן': (1) only חזרה is limited, and שהייה is allowed anyway, as חנניה holds; (2) even שהייה needs גרוף or קטום, and חזרה is certainly forbidden. Steps 9-12 bring a proof from the משנה to decide between them.

steps.title: The משנה has two separate disputes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a proof from the fact that the משנה records two different disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof. The משנה teaches two separate sections. In one, בית שמאי say: hot water but not a cooked dish, and בית הלל say: hot water and a cooked dish. In the other, בית שמאי say: we may remove but not return, and בית הלל say: we may even return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its proof by pointing to the two disputes in the משנה. This step sets up the next move, where it will test each reading of 'לא יתן' against them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on a simple rule: a משנה does not repeat itself for no reason. With two disputes side by side, the גמרא will ask which reading of the משנה lets each one teach something different.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע מִדְּקָתָנֵי תְּרֵי בָבֵי בְּמַתְנִיתִין,
phrases.english: Come and hear: from the fact that two sections are taught in our Mishnah,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: חַמִּין אֲבָל לֹא תַּבְשִׁיל.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: hot water but not a cooked dish.
And Beit Hillel say: hot water and a cooked dish.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹטְלִין אֲבָל לֹא מַחֲזִירִין,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: one may remove but not return,
and Beit Hillel say: one may even return.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע מִדְּקָתָנֵי תְּרֵי בָבֵי בְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the proof that decides between the two readings raised in Steps 6-8.
steps.raayaObject: Whether 'לא יתן' in the משנה refers to leaving or to returning
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two separate disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל in the משנה

steps.title: If the משנה is about leaving, everything fits
steps.stepSummary: If the first part is about שהייה, the first dispute is about what may be left on the stove and the second is about returning. Each dispute teaches something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say the משנה is about leaving a pot on. Then it reads this way: a stove heated with straw or stubble, we may leave a cooked dish on it. If it was heated with גפת or wood, one may not leave it until he sweeps out the coals or covers them with ash. And what may they leave? בית שמאי say: hot water but not a cooked dish. בית הלל say: hot water and a cooked dish. And just as they argue about leaving, they also argue about returning. בית שמאי say: we may remove but not return. בית הלל say: we may even return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the whole משנה as if 'לא יתן' means leaving a pot on. It shows that under this reading, the two disputes cover two different topics.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading the first dispute is about leaving, and the second dispute adds a new topic, returning. Nothing in the משנה is repeated, so this reading flows smoothly.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say
To leave a pot on the stove from before שבת
This is how it teaches. It introduces a reading of the source.

phrases.english: It works well if you say that we learned about leaving,
then this is how it teaches:
A stove that was lit with straw or stubble,
one may leave a cooked dish on it;
with pomace or wood, one may not leave it

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּגְרוֹף, אוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן אֵפֶר.
phrases.english: until he sweeps out the coals, or until he puts ash on them.
And what may they leave?

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: חַמִּין, אֲבָל לֹא תַּבְשִׁיל.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: hot water, but not a cooked dish.
And Beit Hillel say: hot water and a cooked dish.
And just as they argue about leaving,
they also argue about returning,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹטְלִין, אֲבָל לֹא מַחֲזִירִין,
phrases.english: for Beit Shammai say: one may remove, but not return,
and Beit Hillel say: one may even return.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא, לְשַׁהוֹת תְּנַן, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reading from Step 8, that the משנה is about שהייה, against the two disputes introduced in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the משנה is about שהייה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Under this reading, the two disputes cover two different topics, leaving and returning, so neither one is extra.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as being about returning
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא reads the משנה as if the first part is about returning a pot. Then the first dispute is already about returning, and the second dispute says the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the משנה is about returning, then it reads this way: a stove heated with straw or stubble, we may return a cooked dish to it. If it was heated with גפת or wood, one may not return it until he sweeps out the coals or covers them with ash. And what may they return? בית שמאי say: hot water but not a cooked dish. בית הלל say: hot water and a cooked dish. Then: בית שמאי say: we may remove but not return. בית הלל say: we may even return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other reading, that 'לא יתן' means returning a pot. It lays out the whole משנה this way, and this sets up the problem it will point out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading the first dispute is already about what may be returned. So the second dispute, about removing but not returning, covers the same topic again. That repeat is what the next step will attack.

keyTerms.meaning: But, rather. It contrasts with the reading just shown.
To return a pot to the stove on שבת

phrases.english: But if you say that we learned about returning,
then this is how it teaches:
A stove that was lit with straw or stubble,
one may return a cooked dish onto it.
With pomace or wood, one may not return it

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּגְרוֹף אוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן אֵפֶר.
phrases.english: until he sweeps out the coals or until he puts ash on them.
And what may they return?

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: חַמִּין, אֲבָל לֹא תַּבְשִׁיל.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: hot water, but not a cooked dish.
And Beit Hillel say: hot water and a cooked dish.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹטְלִין אֲבָל לֹא מַחֲזִירִין.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: one may remove but not return.
And Beit Hillel say: one may even return.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְהַחֲזִיר תְּנַן, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the opposite reading, that the משנה is about returning, against the same two disputes.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the משנה is about returning
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same two disputes in the משנה, now read under the second interpretation

steps.title: Why would the second dispute be needed?
steps.stepSummary: Under the returning reading, the second dispute is a needless repeat. This seems to show that the משנה is about שהייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then why do I need this second dispute again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that if the משנה is about returning, the second dispute adds nothing new. This is a challenge to the returning reading, and it seems to support the שהייה reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה does not repeat a ruling for no reason. Under the שהייה reading both disputes teach something new, so the challenge seems to favor that reading, the second option from Step 8. This is not the final word, though: on the next amud the גמרא asks whether this is really a difficulty and keeps examining the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This asks what an extra statement adds.

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the two disputes: if 'לא יתן' meant returning, the second dispute would be a repeat. So the proof leans toward reading the משנה as being about שהייה. The גמרא tests this proof further on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof stands, the משנה would not follow חנניה. Leaving food on an unswept stove would then be forbidden even if the food is already cooked like the food of בן דרוסאי. Whether the proof stands is examined on the next amud.

phrases.english: Why do I need this again?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the returning reading from Step 11 by showing it makes the second dispute a repeat.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'לא יתן' in the משנה refers to returning a pot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the dispute about removing but not returning repeats what the first dispute already said. A משנה does not repeat itself for no reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two-disputes proof leans toward reading the משנה as being about שהייה. The גמרא re-examines this proof on the next amud.
